title: Add data_classification metadata to every PII/SPDI field in onfinance_db_model_master/models.py
description: In applications/db-models/repos/onfinance-db-model-master/onfinance_db_model_master/models.py (pinned commit 70b3633e), add a data_classification keyword argument to each field listed in the task 1 map, for example user_email = EmailField(data_classification=["confidential", "pii"]) and zerodha_password = StringField(data_classification=["restricted", "spdi", "pii"]). MongoEngine 0.24.1 stores unknown field kwargs as attributes and raises TypeError if a kwarg name clashes with an existing BaseField attribute, so keep the name data_classification and confirm it is not in dir(BaseField). Also add a module-level docstring comment pointing to docs/data-classification.md. Do not change field types, required/unique flags or collection names, because the change must not alter stored documents. Bump setup.py version to 1.0.1. The library is dev-only (env dev.json) and consumers upgrade by pin.
acceptanceCriteria: python -c "import onfinance_db_model_master.models as m; print(m.User.user_email.data_classification, m.Secrets.zerodha_password.data_classification)" prints the labels from the approved map without error
Every pii/spdi/restricted column in metastore.json catalog db-models-mongodb has a data_classification attribute on the matching models.py field, and a script comparing the two reports zero gaps
git diff on models.py shows only added data_classification kwargs and comments, with no change to field types, required, unique or choices

verificationMethod.description: Re-run probe-schemas for db-models/onfinance-db-model-master at the merged commit. Expected: the SARIF export has no SCH-PII-06 fail result for onfinance_db_model_master/models.py, so fingerprint 3ad57737b286bdf74ce4f42acd9df6dd83c5fe8c3a94e01cc97f8dcb93b57f6e is absent, and the ID.AM.S5 observation for the repo is satisfied.

rootCause.description: models.py was written as plain MongoEngine declarations with no convention for marking sensitive fields, so the PII/SPDI classification in the metastore never reached the code that defines the collections.
